quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: Stressed first syllable: short, open, slightly rounded. It isn't 'cah-'.
quests.explanation: The second syllable has a long vowel that is not part of this pair.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Spelling traps: a can be /ɑː/ (father) or /ɒ/ (want), and ar is nearly always /ɑː/.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: Open the jaw wide in the stressed first syllable.
quests.explanation: Don't let the weak ending raise the first vowel.
quests.vowelTensionRule: The contrast is clearest in stressed syllables; in weak syllables both tend to drift towards a neutral vowel.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: Ea spells a half-open vowel here, as in 'head'.
quests.explanation: Ea behaves as in 'bread' and 'head', so the vowel is short and half open.
quests.vowelTensionRule: A self-check: rest a hand under your chin. The jaw should drop noticeably further for /æ/.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: Stress the first syllable and hold it.
quests.explanation: A common error is shortening the first vowel to 'immail'.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Length misleads here: both vowels lengthen before voiced consonants. Listen for the brighter, tenser colour of /iː/ against the looser /ɪ/.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: A rounded start in the first syllable.
quests.explanation: The second syllable has a different diphthong that isn't part of this choice.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /ɔɪ/ begins with a rounded, back, mid-open vowel; /aɪ/ begins with an unrounded, open one.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: Listen for the syllable that glides: it is the one just before -tion.
quests.explanation: The nearby syllables are weak, so listen for the one carrying the stress.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /eɪ/ glides from mid-front up toward /ɪ/; /e/ is a short, steady half-open vowel.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: The ou spelling; a wide start in the stressed second syllable.
quests.explanation: The initial schwa is weak. The stressed syllable carries the wide-start diphthong.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Both finish with lips rounding. The beginnings differ: ah-like for /aʊ/, schwa-like for /əʊ/.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE VOWEL IN THE SECOND SYLLABLE
quests.hint: The oi sits in the second part of the word. Rounded start.
quests.explanation: The oi spelling points straight to the rounded-start diphthong.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Round the lips at the start for /ɔɪ/. For /aɪ/ the lips stay neutral as the jaw opens.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: Short, open and lightly rounded. Don't hold it.
quests.explanation: A long vowel would add length the word doesn't have.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Raise the back of the tongue and make a clear oval with the lips for /ɔː/. For /ɒ/ drop the jaw and relax.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: Ar plus a consonant: long and open.
quests.explanation: Ar followed by a consonant is a dependable signal, so this word is regular.
quests.vowelTensionRule: If you can hold the vowel indefinitely with an open mouth, it is /ɑː/. /æ/ is quick and bright.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: Ow before er is the open type.
quests.explanation: It follows the same pattern as 'power', with a wide start before the schwa.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Spelling traps: ow can be /aʊ/ (cow) or /əʊ/ (slow), and ou is /aʊ/ in out but /əʊ/ in soul.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: The first vowel is short and central; the p disappears into the b.
quests.explanation: The p+b cluster simplifies to /b/, and the second syllable is weak.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /ɒ/ sits further back and a little lower; /ʌ/ is more central. The tongue moves forward and slightly up from /ɒ/ to /ʌ/.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: Neutral lips in the stressed first syllable, with no rounding.
quests.explanation: U before nd is typical for this vowel, with the lips staying unrounded.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /ʊ/ sits higher and further back; /ʌ/ is lower and more central. Pull the tongue back and round the lips for /ʊ/.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: The ou spelling is the wide-open type. The first syllable is stressed.
quests.explanation: The ending is weak and doesn't change the stressed diphthong.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /aʊ/ starts wide open and closes to a rounded back position; /əʊ/ starts mid-central and closes to the same rounded place.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: Despite the or, this one is short in RP.
quests.explanation: The or here is short, unlike the or in 'fork' or 'horse'.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Spelling cannot decide this one: or before a vowel sound is short in forest and orange but long in chorus and story, so each word must be learned by ear.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: The oo is short here, and the second part has a different vowel.
quests.explanation: The first syllable has the short vowel and 'ball' has another. Check which syllable the pair belongs to.
quests.vowelTensionRule: In a mirror, /uː/ shows a tight forward pout and /ʊ/ a gentle, relaxed circle.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: Both vowels are short. Keep the lips neutral throughout.
quests.explanation: Smiling would turn it into 'sweeming', so keep the lips relaxed.
quests.vowelTensionRule: The jaw drops slightly more for /ɪ/ than for /iː/. If your /ɪ/ is turning into /iː/, relax the lips and lower the tongue a little.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE VOWEL IN THE FIRST SYLLABLE
quests.hint: In the stressed first syllable, keep the jaw half open.
quests.explanation: Stress falls on ten-, which has the half-open vowel. The second syllable holds a weak vowel that sounds quite different.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Duration is similar, so rely on openness: a small mouth gap for /ɪ/, a slightly larger one for /e/.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: The ew spells /juː/, with a glide before the vowel.
quests.explanation: The long vowel is preceded by a /j/ glide in RP.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Short oo words (book, good, foot) take /ʊ/, long ones (food, moon) take /uː/. No spelling rule separates them, so group them by sound.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: Open the jaw and keep the lips neutral on the first vowel.
quests.explanation: Long, open and unrounded. The short vowel would be rounded.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /ɑː/ is long, open and unrounded; /ɒ/ is short, open and lightly rounded.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: The our spelling hides a steady central vowel.
quests.explanation: Ou plus r gives a steady vowel here but the long rounded vowel in 'four' and 'pour'.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Both are long, so duration is no help. Listen for the darker, rounder colour of /ɔː/ against the flatter /ɜː/.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: The a is long and gliding.
quests.explanation: The -ment ending is weak, so the stress is on the glide in the first syllable.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Say /e/ with no movement. For /eɪ/ let the jaw rise and the tongue slide upward towards the end.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: Ow before er opens wide first, as in 'power'.
quests.explanation: It follows the same pattern as 'shower' and 'power'.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Only /aʊ/ opens the jaw wide at the start. /əʊ/ begins relaxed and rounds the lips more steadily.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: A short vowel with a small mouth gap. The dg is just /dʒ/.
quests.explanation: Opening the jaw would sound like 'bredge', so keep the gap small.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Keep the lips relaxed for /ɪ/, not stretched as for /iː/. /e/ is only a half-open smile.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: A /j/ glide first, then a long rounded vowel. Don't clip it.
quests.explanation: The long rounded vowel follows the /mj/ glide.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /uː/ is the highest, furthest-back vowel; /ʊ/ is slightly lower and more central, so the tongue relaxes forward.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: The ai spelling points to a rising glide, so don't open the jaw wide.
quests.explanation: Spelled ai, it glides upward. The word 'pint' would start with an open jaw instead.
quests.vowelTensionRule: The jaw starts lower for /aɪ/ and visibly closes. /eɪ/ starts nearly half closed and moves less.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: The word ends on a long, open vowel after a silent u.
quests.explanation: The silent u and the weak initial vowel are not part of this choice.
quests.vowelTensionRule: BATH words (class, path, plant, dance, half) are one of the biggest differences between RP and other accents. Follow the RP set.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: Ea is short here: half open.
quests.explanation: Ea is short here, unlike in 'break', where it glides.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Both are short, so the only question is how high the front of the tongue rises.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: A quick first syllable, then a /j/ glide into a long vowel.
quests.explanation: The first syllable is a weak schwa, and the long vowel follows /mj/.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Before dark /l/ the contrast gets muddy ('pull' versus 'pool'), so use lip protrusion and length together.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: A rising glide: the a_e pattern again, with the jaw closing.
quests.explanation: The a_e signals a glide that rises towards /ɪ/.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Movement plus length: /eɪ/ is longer and travels, /e/ is short and static.
